anti_overlap: Focuses on spatial importance weighting from medical imaging, not format optimization (SVG) or tokenization (encoding)
decision_lens: Asks 'would a radiologist make the same diagnosis from the compressed image?' — maps to 'would the LLM make the same decision from the compressed terminal state?'
distance_rationale: Both domains compress rich visual information while preserving decision-critical features, but medical imaging has 30+ years of research on exactly which features matter.
expected_isomorphisms: Region-of-interest encoding and perceptual lossless compression directly map to terminal state compression — most of the screen is static, and the decision-relevant parts are small.
focus: Diagnostic image compression — preserving clinically significant features while dramatically reducing data
name: fd-medical-imaging-compression
persona: Medical imaging informaticist who works with DICOM, lossy compression for radiology, and understands which visual features are diagnostically significant vs. noise
review_areas: Region-of-interest encoding — high fidelity for diagnostically significant regions, aggressive compression elsewhere (maps to: high fidelity for active UI elements, low for static chrome)
Perceptual lossless vs. mathematically lossless — acceptable degradation that doesn't change clinical decisions
DICOM metadata as companion channel — structured metadata travels alongside the image, not embedded in it
Progressive resolution — send a low-res version first, enhance on demand
Windowing and level — the same raw data rendered differently for different diagnostic questions (maps to: same terminal state rendered differently for different agent tasks)

severity_examples.condition: Error text in a status bar gets truncated as 'static chrome'
severity_examples.scenario: Compressing away the diagnostically significant region

severity_examples.condition: Always sending maximum detail when low-res would suffice for most turns

success_hints: Proposes a region-of-interest approach where active/important terminal areas get higher fidelity
task_context: Terminal screens, like medical images, have regions of varying diagnostic importance. Most of the screen is static chrome; the semantically important parts are concentrated.
